channel.title: Life in the Simulation
channel.description: Essays, field guides and thought experiments about simulation theory, consciousness, artificial intelligence, attention and living deliberately in a mediated world.

item.title: The Feeling of Understanding Is Not Understanding
item.description: Why fluent explanations feel like knowledge, how that confidence fails under pressure, and a practical test for whether your mental model can actually do work.

item.title: Password Managers Without the Hype: Bitwarden vs 1Password vs Proton Pass vs KeePassXC
item.description: A practical password-manager comparison for individuals and families, including security tradeoffs, recovery planning, migration steps and the no-buy option.

item.title: Dreams Are Not Evidence That Reality Is Simulated
item.description: Dreams show that experience can feel worldlike without tracking the waking environment. That is important evidence about minds—not proof of a simulated universe.

item.title: E-Ink Writing Tablets for Focus: reMarkable vs Supernote vs BOOX
item.description: A no-hype decision guide to reMarkable Paper Pro, Supernote Manta and BOOX Note Air5 C—plus the honest case for buying nothing.

item.title: A Model Can Be Right for the Wrong Reason
item.description: Why an AI model can score well, sound convincing and still rely on shortcuts that fail when the world changes—and how to judge it more honestly.

item.title: The Best Books to Understand AI Without the Hype
item.description: A five-book AI reading path covering how the technology works, where it fails, alignment, power, labor and the people living with automated decisions.

item.title: Meaning After Automation
item.description: If machines reduce the need for effort, meaning will not automatically disappear—but we may have to stop confusing difficulty with value.

item.title: The Attention Economy Is a Reality Engine
item.description: Competition for attention does more than consume time. It influences which events become vivid, which identities get rehearsed and which futures feel possible.

item.title: When the Internet Is Full of AI Agents
item.description: The next trust problem is not just synthetic content. It is synthetic participants acting, negotiating and speaking at machine speed.

item.title: The Extended Mind Is Already Here
item.description: Phones, notebooks and AI tools do not merely store information. They increasingly participate in the loops through which people remember, decide and act.

item.title: Is the Universe Made of Information?
item.description: Information is indispensable for describing physics. Whether it is the substance of reality is a deeper—and often confused—claim.

item.title: What Would Count as Evidence That Reality Is Simulated?
item.description: A useful theory must risk being wrong. Here is how to separate testable predictions from anomalies that only feel suggestive.

item.title: The Real World Is Becoming a Premium Experience
item.description: As synthetic experience becomes cheaper and more abundant, unmediated presence may become one of the scarce goods.

item.title: The Scoreboards We Mistake for Life
item.description: Money, followers, ratings and productivity are useful abstractions—until the measure begins replacing the thing it was meant to represent.

item.title: Consciousness Is Still the Weird Part
item.description: Whatever reality is made of, subjective experience remains one of its strangest and most immediate facts.

item.title: AI and the End of Knowing Who Made What
item.description: When text, images, voices and video can be synthesized cheaply, trust shifts from appearance toward source, context and provenance.

item.title: Your Algorithm Is Becoming Your Reality
item.description: Recommendation systems do more than predict preference. Repeated selection can become the environment through which a person experiences the world.

item.title: The Simulation Hypothesis Without the Hype
item.description: A sober look at the famous probability argument, the assumptions underneath it, and why the question remains useful even without a verdict.
